news_headline: Scoop: DOJ, TikTok settle for $400 million in children's privacy suit
post_text:
On August 21, the Justice Department announced a $400 million settlement with TikTok and ByteDance, resolving a 2024 COPPA lawsuit alleging the platform collected children's personal data without proper consent. TikTok pays without admitting wrongdoing, $300 million up front and $100 million deferred. The DOJ called it one of the largest recoveries ever obtained under federal children's privacy law.

This is not a one-off fine. It's the latest in a sustained US government campaign against TikTok that has already included a divest-or-ban law, Supreme Court review, and a forced ownership restructuring. Other consumer platforms with teen audiences are watching closely: the settlement makes clear that children's data practices carry nine-figure regulatory exposure.

WBR's piece on TikTok argued exactly this, that the pressure building around the app's US operations carries consequences well beyond any single enforcement action. The $400M settlement is a concrete proof point. Read the full analysis on the WBR website.

#TikTok #BigTech
